item.title: Good for the Business, the Employee and the Customer: Breaking the Zero-Sum Game of Service
item.description: Photo source: Interactive Powers Good for the Business, the Employee and the Customer: Breaking the Zero-Sum Game of Service Customer service has three actors: 🏢 the business, 👩‍💻 the employee and 🙋 the customer. For years, improving things for one of them meant that someone else paid the bill. Try it with any process and you’ll see it almost always holds — even with AI or digital tools, someone loses:

item.title: The Branch With a Queue and the Branch Standing Empty Are the Same Network
item.description: Photo source: Interactive Powers The Branch With a Queue and the Branch Standing Empty Are the Same Network An 8-branch network, one business day, 1,723 visits. 229 customers leave without being served: 13.3% of all visits. That same day, the in-person positions add up to 120 hours with nobody in front of them: 31% of installed capacity. A queue and an empty seat, at the same time, in the same network.
